subject.title: fix(shared): cap backtick delimiter length to prevent unbounded repeat

question: For oversized backtick-heavy content, should the shared helper preserve exact content with a matching delimiter, reject or truncate at a defined input limit, or switch to another supported encoding?
rationale: A bounded Markdown delimiter cannot preserve arbitrary exact backtick content under the current string-returning contract, so the safe failure and compatibility behavior requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Bound the input contract
options.body: Define and test a maximum input size before formatting, then reject or truncate oversized content while retaining longer-than-content delimiters for accepted input.

options.title: Keep exact-content behavior
options.body: Retain the current dynamic delimiter because output growth is linear in already-present input and containment remains correct.

options.title: Adopt another encoding
options.body: Change callers to an explicitly supported HTML or transport-specific code representation with compatibility proof across consumers.

recommendation.title: Bound the input contract
recommendation.body: Define and test a maximum input size before formatting, then reject or truncate oversized content while retaining longer-than-content delimiters for accepted input.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes a shared formatting contract and should route through the strongest available shared-runtime owner.
